facts.claim: Foreverland (Italy) raised a €6M ($7M) Series A in March 2026, led by Kost Capital and Maia Ventures, taking its total funding to €9.4M.
Win-Win Foods raised a £3M (~$4M) Series A in July 2025, led by Oetker Collection and FoodLabs, to scale cocoa-free chocolate production and expand across Europe.

Green Spot Technologies raised €5M ($5.8M) in a Series A on 6 November 2025, led by Team for the Planet, to scale upcycled fermented cocoa-alternative ingredients from 100 to 1,000 tonnes/year under its new Milatea brand.
Voyage Foods closed a $3.25M Series B-II round on 18 December 2025, adding to prior 2024/2025 rounds that bring its total disclosed funding to roughly $91-113M.

Cargill and Voyage Foods launched NextCoa, a grapeseed-based cocoa-free confectionery ingredient, into the North American market on 12 May 2026, marking Cargill's entry into the cocoa-alternative race.

Global agrifoodtech venture funding was roughly flat at $16.2B in 2025 (down 3% year-over-year per AgFunder), with capital increasingly concentrated in companies with tangible science and clear paths to revenue, the backdrop against which alt-cocoa raises are being priced.

Kost Capital and Maia Ventures co-led Foreverland's €6M Series A (March 2026), with first-time participation from CDP Venture Capital, Riello Investimenti SGR's Linfa agrifoodtech fund and Newtree Impact.
Oetker Collection and FoodLabs led Win-Win Foods' £3M ($4M) Series A (July 2025), joined by food-industry strategics Paulig, plus Mustard Seed Maze, Gota Ventures and Kapital.

Team for the Planet led Green Spot Technologies' €5M ($5.8M) Series A (November 2025) to scale its upcycled, fermented cocoa-alternative ingredient line, backed by EIT Food and the European Innovation Council.

facts.claim: The EU Council agreed in December 2025 to postpone the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) — which requires cocoa traders and brands to prove deforestation-free sourcing post-2020 — by another year, to 30 December 2026.

As of early 2026 no precision-fermentation- or cell-culture-derived food ingredient (including cell-cultured cocoa) had received EU Novel Food approval, with the process typically taking 2.5-4+ years, versus several such approvals already granted in the US.

The EU's Biotech Act, finalized in late 2025, explicitly excludes novel foods (including cell-cultured ingredients) from its new regulatory-sandbox provisions on ethical/cultural grounds, removing a potential fast-track for cell-cultured cocoa in Europe.

Cocoa futures corrected more than 70% from their late-2024 highs and fell over 30% in early 2026, as the ICCO projected the 2025/26 season would swing from a ~500,000-tonne deficit to a ~150,000-tonne surplus on improved West African and Ecuador harvests, easing some price pressure toward cocoa-free substitution.
The ICCO projects the 2026/27 cocoa surplus will shrink sharply to just ~80,000 tonnes, down from ~415,000 tonnes in 2025/26, pointing to renewed supply tightness after the 2026 price correction.

players.name: Cargill

players.name: Nestlé
players.evidence: Launched its Choco Crossies 'Snack Vibes' line in Germany (announced March 2026) formulated with 74% Planet A Foods' ChoViva, its first cocoa-free confectionery product.

players.name: Puratos (Sparkalis)
players.evidence: Corporate venture arm Sparkalis invested in cell-cultured cocoa startup California Cultured and is set to launch the first professional cell-based-cocoa chocolate for US B2B customers by end of 2026.

players.name: Lindt
players.evidence: Kept up its multi-year cocoa-free push via ChoViva (Planet A Foods), maintaining a long-term commercial relationship through 2025-2026 as ChoViva also scaled to Nestlé and Barry Callebaut.
